panels.head: How the pieces stack up
panels.caption: A request arrives at the edge, is routed at the entry tier, handled by compute, and reads or writes state in the data tier. Identity, keys, metrics and templates cut across all four.
panels.side: a request travels top to bottom

panels.head: Compute — where code runs
panels.caption: The choice is how much of the machine you want to stop thinking about, from a whole virtual server down to a single function.

items.note: Virtual machines you rent. Billed per second after the first minute.

items.label: Lambda
items.note: Run a function, no server to manage. Hard 15-minute ceiling per run.

items.label: ECS
items.note: Runs containers using AWS's own scheduler. No Kubernetes to learn.

items.label: EKS
items.note: Managed Kubernetes control plane. You still pay for the worker nodes.

items.label: Fargate
items.note: Containers with no EC2 underneath. You size the task, not the machine.

items.label: ECR
items.note: Private registry for your container images. ECS and EKS pull from it.

items.label: Auto Scaling
items.note: Adds and removes instances to track demand. Replaces unhealthy ones too.

panels.head: Storage — where bytes sit
panels.caption: Four different shapes of storage. Picking the wrong one is usually a cost problem rather than a correctness one.

items.note: Object storage for files of any size. Eleven nines of durability.

items.label: EBS
items.note: A virtual disk attached to one EC2. Lives in a single Availability Zone.

items.label: EFS
items.note: A shared file system many servers mount at once. Grows on its own.

items.label: Glacier
items.note: Archive storage priced to be forgotten. Retrieval takes minutes to hours.

panels.head: Databases — where state lives
panels.caption: Relational when the shape of the data matters, key-value when scale and latency matter, a cache in front when reads dominate.

items.label: RDS
items.note: Managed relational databases. Patching and backups handled for you.

items.label: Aurora
items.note: AWS's own MySQL and Postgres engine. Storage grows as you write.
Key-value store, no servers. Single-digit millisecond reads at scale.

items.label: ElastiCache
items.note: Managed Redis or Memcached. Sits in front of a database to absorb reads.

items.label: Redshift
items.note: Warehouse for analytics. Columnar storage, built for very large scans.

panels.head: Networking and delivery
panels.caption: The path a request takes before it reaches your code: name lookup, edge cache, filtering, load balancing, then the API front door.

items.note: Your own private network inside AWS. Nothing reaches in until you allow it.

items.label: Route 53
items.note: DNS and domain registration. Named after DNS port 53.

items.label: CloudFront
items.note: Caches content close to your users and terminates TLS at the edge.

items.label: ELB
items.note: Spreads traffic across healthy targets and drops any that fail a check.

items.label: API Gateway
items.note: Front door for APIs. Throttling and auth without writing either.

items.label: Transit Gateway
items.note: One hub joining many VPCs and on-prem links, instead of a mesh of peerings.

items.label: Direct Connect
items.note: A private physical line into AWS. Predictable latency, no public internet.

panels.head: Analytics and AI
panels.caption: Getting data in, querying it where it already sits, and putting a model in front of it. Bedrock is the one most teams reach for first now.

items.label: Kinesis
items.note: Ingests streaming events in real time, before anything is stored.

items.label: Glue
items.note: Catalogues your data and runs the jobs that reshape it.

items.label: Athena
items.note: SQL straight over files in S3. No cluster, priced per byte scanned.

items.label: EMR
items.note: Managed Spark and Hadoop clusters for heavy processing.

items.label: SageMaker
items.note: Build, train and host your own machine-learning models.
Foundation models behind one API, including Anthropic's Claude.

panels.head: Security and identity
panels.caption: IAM decides every call in your account. The rest narrow the blast radius when something does get through.

items.note: Who may do what, to which resource. An explicit deny always wins.

items.label: KMS
items.note: Managed encryption keys. Key material never leaves the service in the clear.

items.label: Cognito
items.note: Sign-up and sign-in for your app's users. Issues tokens your API verifies.

items.label: WAF
items.note: Filters malicious web requests. Sits in front of CloudFront or a load balancer.

items.label: GuardDuty
items.note: Watches logs for suspicious behaviour. It reports findings, it does not block.

items.label: Secrets Manager
items.note: Stores and rotates credentials. Apps fetch at runtime instead of hardcoding.

panels.head: Messaging, events and operations
panels.caption: The glue between services, plus the two things you will want the first time something breaks in production.

items.label: SQS
items.note: A queue holding work until something takes it. A consumer can fail safely.

items.label: SNS
items.note: Publishes one message to many subscribers at once. Fan-out, not a queue.

items.label: EventBridge
items.note: Routes events between services by rule, including events from SaaS apps.

items.label: Step Functions
items.note: Orchestrates steps as a state machine. Retries and branching without glue.
Metrics, logs and alarms. Almost everything reports here by default.

items.label: CloudFormation
items.note: Your infrastructure as a template. Rolls the whole stack back on failure.

panels.head: Governance, audit and recovery
panels.caption: The account-level layer. Boring until an audit, an incident, or a bill that nobody can explain.

items.note: Records every API call in the account. The first place to look after an incident.

items.label: Config
items.note: Tracks how each resource is configured and flags drift from your rules.

items.label: Organizations
items.note: Many accounts under one root, with guardrails and one bill.

items.label: Security Hub
items.note: Collects findings from GuardDuty, Config and others into one view.

items.label: ACM
items.note: Issues and renews TLS certificates for free. Renewal is automatic.

items.label: Backup
items.note: One backup policy across EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS and more.
